parties:
Kazi Nafiul Majid ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, Jessore, and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The case of the Petitioner Kazi Nafiul Majid is that he passed S.S.C. Examination from St. Joseph High School, Khulna, in first Division. Thereafter, he got himself admitted in H.S.C. (Science) course in B.L. College, Daulatpur, completed his course and filled up form to sit for the H.S.C. examination from there, but due to transfer of his father Kazi Lokman Hossain to Babuganj Upazila as Upazila Nirbahi Officer, he got his examination centre transferred to Babuganj, Rukhedia Centre and sat for examination there, held in June, 1988. The Petitioner being ill, he was allowed to sit in sick bed and he accordingly completed examination from sick bed except second paper physics on the last date. During examination there was no allegation of adopting unfair means. He stood 10th in the said examination securing 861 marks. Thereafter, the petitioner joined Bangladesh Army as a commissioned officer in 24th B.M.A. long course on 16.7.89. While he had been following the course he received Memo. No. Go JR-B 806 dated 28.10.89 (Annexure A to the petition) issued by the respondent No. 2, the Controller of Examination, asking him to show cause why the result of his H.S.C. Examination should not be cancelled and he should not be expelled for 6 years, on certain allegation. The petitioner accordingly showed causes denying the allegations. Thereafter, the petitioner came to know that his H.S.C. result was cancelled by the impugned order and he was debarred from sitting for H.S.C. Examination for the years 1989 and 1990 by the respondent Board as communicated by the respondent No. 2 by the impugned memorandum. The petitioner was never informed that there was an inquiry committee nor he was shown any document nor the names of the witnesses were disclosed to him. He was not given any opportunity of being heard personally or to see the evidence. He was also not given opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses or to confront them. The report of the Committee was arbitrary, illegal and without lawful authority. The case of the petitioner is not covered by regulation 157 of the relevant Regulations as neither the invigilator nor the officer-in-charge of the centre nor the Head Examiner reported against him and as such the impugned punishment was inflicted against the petitioner without lawful authority. The impugned action, after the result was published and the petitioner was granted certificate, is unlawful and his vested right to hold the certificate cannot be taken away. The impugned action was malafide and it was taken for collateral purposes at the instance of the enemies of his father. One Mr. Atiur Rahman, Professor of M.M. Collage, Jessore, was behind the scene. 

 6. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that although the Board has authority to cancel the certificate, but as there is no regulation for withdrawing certificate, the proceeding itself is void. He further submits that after the result is published no action can be taken for its cancellation. He also submits that regulation 157 of the connected Regulations is for taking action for adopting unfairmeans before the result is published where the candidate is suspected to have adopted unfairmeans, if reported against by the invigilator of Officer-in-Charge of the Centre and as there was no report against the petitioner during continuance of the examination, no action can be taken against him. He has drawn our attention to regulation 157 of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore, and Section 18(2) (viii) of the Intermediate & Secondary Education Ordinance, 1961, and Section 39(2Xiii) of the said Ordinance. Under Section 18(2Xviii), power has been conferred to the Board to grant certificates to persons who have passed examination held by the Board and to withdraw certificates from them. Mr. Khondker submits that under Section 39 (2) (iii), the Board has given power to frame regulation for granting and withholding certificates, but there is no provision for making regulation for withdrawal of certificates and so, after the result is finally published, the Board has no authority to cancel the result of the examination or to withdraw the certificate or to award any other punishment in this connection. He further submits that in any view of the matter, the petitioner having not been given the opportunity to cross-examine the witness on the basis of whose deposition the punishment was awarded, the principle of natural justice was violated and on that ground also the punishment is unauthorised. 

 9. So, it appears from Section 39(1) that the Board has power to make any regulation for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the Ordinance generally though some particular subjects are enumerated in Section 39(2) which are not exhaustive. Moreover, Section 39(2)(iii) empowers the Board to frame regulations for granting and withholding of certificate. Withholding of certificate is obviously for a temporary period and ultimately either it will be granted or withdrawn. So it cannot be said that the Board has no authority to withdraw certificate. Hence, although no regulation for withdrawing certificate, in particular, has been framed, the Board is not powerless if unfairmeans is found to have been adopted and it is detected after the result Is published and the certificate is granted as the law has given it power to do so. In the Regulations framed, some procedures to deal with the situation arisen out of reported unfairmeans in the examination hail are there. Regulation 157 of the said Regulations contain Discipline Rules in case of suspected commission of unfairmeans. It is mentioned in paragraph 2 of regulation 157(d), "Any case not falling within the above Rules shall be decided by the Board in accordance with the nature of offence on the recommendation of Discipline Committee." 

 11. The petitioner appeared in the H.S.C. Examination in 1988. He stood 10th therein. After his result was published, an enquiry committee was set up and it appears that the petitioner was asked to show cause why the result of his examination should not be cancelled for adopting unfairmeans. The petitioner showed causes and was given personal hearing by the said committee which after considering his reply and examining witnesses and perusing necessary papers and documents submitted a report (Annexure X to the affidavit-in-opposition No.2) to the respondent Board finding the petitioner guilty of adopting unfairmeans in the said examination and for that purpose in a planned way he got his examination centre transferred to Babuganj by misrepresentation of facts and he managed to sit in a separate room on the ground of illness al though he was not ill due to influence of his father who was Upazila Nirbahi Officer of Babuganj at the relevant time and at the active aid of his father he committed the said offence and thereby secured high marks. Thereafter, the petitioner was again asked to show cause why his examination should not be cancelled on the charges found by the enquiry committee and why he should not be debarred from appearing in such examination for the next 5 years. In the show cause notice, details of charges as found by the enquiry committee were mentioned. 

 16. So it appears that the impugned order was passed by the respondent Board in accordance with law after compliance with the requirements of the principle of natural justice and after getting the matter enquired into by an Enquiry Committee which submitted the report after hearing the petitioner in person and considering his explanation and after giving him another opportunity to show cause before passing the impugned order and considering his reply thereto. Besides the Enquiry Committee, the matter was considered by the discipline committee and the examination committee and finally by the Board.
